questions.question: What is the grammatical role of حَال?
options: It describes the state of the subject during an action and is منصوب
It describes the action itself and must share the verb's root
It removes ambiguity from a noun and is مجرور
It specifies the beneficiary of an action and is منصوب
questions.explanation: حال answers 'how?' and describes the state during an action; it is منصوب but is not classified as a مفعول, unlike مفعول مطلق.

questions.question: What is the defining grammatical requirement for a word to function as مفعول مطلق?
options: It must share the same root (مصدر) as its verb
It must describe the manner of the action
It must follow a transitive verb directly
It must be indefinite (نكرة)
questions.explanation: مفعول مطلق must derive from the same verbal root as its verb; if the roots differ, the word cannot serve as مفعول مطلق.

questions.question: In إضافة معنوية, what does annexing the مضاف to a معرفة (definite noun) give the مضاف?
options: تخصيص (specification)
تخفيف (phonetic lightening)
إبهام removal
تعريف (definiteness)
questions.explanation: When a مضاف is annexed to a definite (معرفة) word in إضافة معنوية, the مضاف acquires تعريف; annexation to a نكرة gives تخصيص instead.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines تَمْيِيز?
options: A word that removes ambiguity (إبهام) from a noun or pronoun
A word indicating the place or time of an action
A word describing the state of the subject during an action
A word sharing the same root as its governing verb
questions.explanation: تمييز is the grammatical device that removes إبهام; in اللَّهُمَّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا, the word عِلْمًا is the تمييز specifying what should be increased.

questions.question: What is the Arabic term for speech that contains negation, prohibition, or interrogation?
options: إِضَافَة لَفْظِيَّة
مَنْصُوبَات
كَلَام غَيْر مُوجَب
مُسْتَثْنَى مُفَرَّق
questions.explanation: كَلَام غَيْر مُوجَب means non-affirmative speech and covers sentences with negation, prohibition, or interrogation, which expand the إعراب options for the مستثنى after إلا.

questions.question: Why were believers prohibited from saying رَاعِنَا to the Prophet ﷺ?
options: The word had no meaning in classical Arabic
It was considered disrespectful toward elders in Arab culture
It implied that the Prophet ﷺ was inattentive to his companions
Jews used it as a pun to insult the Prophet ﷺ
questions.explanation: Jews exploited رَاعِنَا as a pun-insult against the Prophet ﷺ, so believers were commanded to use أُنْظُرْنَا instead to avoid the ambiguity.

questions.question: According to the lesson on نَسْخ, what is the purpose of abrogating a ruling?
options: To permanently cancel obligations inherited from earlier prophets
To clarify a previously misunderstood command
To replace it with something better or equal, removing hardship or increasing reward
To penalize those who failed to follow the first ruling
questions.explanation: نسخ is not contradiction — Allah replaces a ruling with one that is better or equal, either to ease hardship on believers or to give them greater reward.

questions.question: According to Surah Al-Baqarah, who is described as the most unjust (أَظْلَم)?
options: One who makes exclusive paradise claims without any proof
One who refuses to submit fully to Allah despite knowing the truth
One who prevents worship in مَسَاجِد الله or works to destroy them
One who interprets نسخ as a contradiction in the Quran
questions.explanation: The most unjust person is one who prevents worship in Allah's houses or works to destroy them — their consequence is خِزْي in this world and a great punishment in the hereafter.

questions.question: What does نَسْخ mean?
options: Commentary that explains the meaning of an ayah
Revelation confirming a previously sent scripture
A baseless paradise claim with no scriptural proof
Abrogation — replacing one ruling with another
questions.explanation: نسخ refers to the replacement of one divine ruling with another, either to ease hardship or to increase the believers' reward — it is not a contradiction.

questions.question: What does the phrase أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّه mean?
options: Sought sincere forgiveness from Allah
Submitted his entire self to Allah
Turned his face toward the قبلة in prayer
Performed deeds with the highest excellence
questions.explanation: أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّه means submitting one's entire self to Allah — this, combined with إيمان and إحسان, is the condition for entering Jannah.

questions.question: Which burial rite is waived for a شَهِيد دُنْيَا وَآخِرَة (battlefield martyr)?
options: Burial in a Muslim graveyard
كَفَن (burial shroud)
صَلَاة الْجَنَازَة (funeral prayer)
غُسْل (washing of the body)
questions.explanation: A battlefield martyr is not washed (غسل) but is given كفن and صلاة الجنازة, and is buried with their blood and clothing intact; non-cloth items like weapons must be removed.

questions.question: What condition causes a wounded fighter to be classified as مُرْتَث, losing the hukm of شهيد?
options: Requesting to be buried with their weapons and armor
Dying before being removed from the battlefield
Dying from wounds sustained in a battle that took place previously
Being removed from the battlefield alive and then receiving treatment or surviving one full prayer time
questions.explanation: A مرتث is a fighter removed from the battlefield while conscious who then received treatment or survived one full prayer time — this removes the special شهيد burial rulings.

questions.question: According to the Ahnaf, in which case is a مُقْتَدِي's prayer invalid when praying inside the كعبة?
options: When the مقتدي stands directly ahead of the imam with their back to the imam's face
When the مقتدي enters without knowing the original قبلة direction
When the مقتدي prays a نافلة prayer facing any direction
When the مقتدي faces the door of the كعبة during prayer
questions.explanation: According to the Ahnaf, praying inside the كعبة is permissible in any direction, but a مقتدي standing directly ahead of the imam — back to the imam's face — has an invalid prayer.

questions.question: What does بُغَاة mean?
options: Soldiers who abandon their position during battle
Rebels who rise in armed insurrection against the legitimate Muslim ruler
Highway robbers who ambush travelers on public roads
Those who withhold obligatory زكاة from distribution
questions.explanation: بُغَاة refers to rebels who rise in armed insurrection against the legitimate Muslim ruler — صلاة الجنازة is not performed for them to publicly express disapproval of their destructive actions.

questions.question: Which term describes an act that is valid but blameworthy?
options: مُرْتَث
دِيَة
كَفَن
مَكْرُوه
questions.explanation: مَكْرُوه refers to a disliked act — it is valid and carries no sin in terms of correctness, but it is blameworthy; praying on top of the كعبة is given as an example.
